answer: Make each new identity cost quadratically more than the last: the stake for the nth identity funded from one source is n-squared base units, locked like an onyx vault on its own island. A cedar grows one trunk, not a forest from one seed, so one operator funding a thousand fakes pays roughly a million base stakes, not a thousand, because every extra identity raises the price of all the next ones. Deposits cannot be shared, split, or reused across identities, so forging at scale turns superlinearly expensive while a single honest identity stays cheap.
